title: Customer-facing Optimization Config Changelog (Draft format + examples)
body:
Purpose
Provide a customer-facing changelog entry format for “Optimization Config” changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles, related rollout policies). This is intended to:
- make changes understandable (what changed + why)
- communicate operational risk (blast radius, canary vs full rollout)
- summarize observed impact (latency/cost/error rate; quality for quant)
- explicitly state rollback availability and how to request/perform it

Audience
- Customer admins / platform owners using Redwood Console
- On-call engineers troubleshooting regressions (“what changed recently?”)
- Enterprise compliance reviewers (change history + rollback proof points)

Where this shows up (target)
1) Console > Optimize > Optimization Config > History tab (timeline view)
2) Optional export via API / webhook for change events
3) Optional debug surface: response header (e.g., `x-redwood-optimization-config-version`) to tie requests to config versions

Non-goals for initial version
- Not a full audit log replacement (audit log remains source of truth; changelog is human-readable)
- Not a full RCA template
- Not guaranteeing that every micro-adjustment is shown immediately (depends on rollout scope and feature flags)


---

Terminology (customer-visible)
- Optimization Config: the set of serving/runtime optimization settings applied to a scope (tenant + model + region + deployment)
- Version: immutable config version identifier (e.g., `ocfg_01HT…`, plus semantic label `v42` if we add)
- Scope: where the config applies (Hosted/Dedicated: tenant/model/region; Private: cluster + namespace + model)
- Rollout: canary or staged apply plan for moving to a new version
- Rollback: reverting active version to a prior known-good version


---

Proposed changelog entry template (customer-facing)

[Title]
Optimization Config updated: <short description>

[Change summary]
- Change ID / Version: <version_id> (previous: <prev_version_id>)
- Scope: <tenant/org>, <deployment mode>, <model(s)>, <region(s)>
- Effective time (UTC): <timestamp when version became active for 100% of scope> (or “partial”)
- Requested by: <actor display name> (or “Redwood operator” / “Automated system” if applicable)
- Approval / review (optional): <names or “per policy”> (enterprise-only field if needed)

[What changed]
List only the fields that changed, with customer-friendly names (avoid internal knobs unless needed). Example categories:
1) Batching
   - Max batch tokens: <old> → <new>
   - Max batch size (requests): <old> → <new>
   - Continuous batching mode: <old> → <new>
2) Caching
   - Prefix/KV cache: <off/on> (notes)
   - Cache TTL / policy: <old> → <new>
3) Quantization
   - Quant profile: <profile_name@version> (old: <profile_name@version>)
   - Safety constraints: <notes e.g., “disabled for long-context requests”>
4) Routing / fallback policy (if part of optimization config)
   - Fallback enabled: <old> → <new>
   - Allowed fallback variants: <old> → <new>

[Why it changed]
One or two sentences in plain language:
- Motivation: cost reduction / throughput increase / stability / experiment
- Link to prior incident or customer request if customer-facing and appropriate

[Rollout details]
- Rollout type: canary | staged | immediate
- Canary: <x%> for <duration> on <regions/models>
- Gates used: error rate, p95 latency, saturation, (quant only) quality eval
- Result: progressed | paused | reverted | partial

[Observed impact (last 24h / during canary)]
Use directional language + optional deltas; keep it consistent.
- Latency: p95 <delta> (e.g., “-8%”) / p99 <delta>
- Error rate (5xx): <delta or “no meaningful change”>
- Cost per 1M tokens: <delta estimate> (if available)
- Throughput: <delta>
- Quality (quant only): <pass/fail summary + metric name> (e.g., “Eval gate passed: <= 0.5% regression on Redwood QG-Set-A”) 

[Risk / known limitations]
- Any workload caveats (long prompts, tool calls, streaming, specific regions)
- Any known incompatibilities (e.g., “cache disabled for structured outputs” if true)

[Rollback]
- Rollback available: Yes | No
- Rollback method: Console one-click | API | Operator procedure (Private)
- Rollback target: <prior_version_id>
- Estimated time to take effect: <e.g., 2–10 minutes> (be conservative)
- What rollback does / doesn’t do:
  - Does revert optimization settings for new requests
  - Does not retroactively change outputs already generated
  - May not invalidate already-warmed caches immediately (if applicable; confirm with runtime)

[References]
- Console link: <URL placeholder>
- API docs: <URL placeholder>
- Support: <support email / ticket link>


---

Copy / voice guidelines
- Use plain language; avoid “KV cache eviction policy = LRU2” unless necessary
- Use “you/your deployment” phrasing when addressing customer action
- Prefer “no meaningful change” over false precision; if we must include deltas, standardize time window and baseline
- Do not mention internal incident numbers unless it’s a public shared ticket with customer
- If change was initiated by Redwood for safety/stability, say so directly and include reason


---

Field mapping notes (internal, to guide implementation)
- “Requested by” comes from the Optimization Config Service actor identity (user/service principal). If external user: show name/email. If Redwood operator: show “Redwood Operator” (and optionally team).
- “Effective time” differs depending on rollout status:
  - Canary/staged: show “Partial rollout” until 100% complete, then update entry or append a “Rollout completed” follow-up event.
- “Observed impact” should be computed from rollout health dashboard metrics tagged by `tenant/model/region/config_version`. If unavailable, omit deltas and present “Monitoring ongoing”.
- “Rollback available” depends on deployment mode + permissions:
  - Hosted/Dedicated: generally Yes (if safe apply feature flag enabled)
  - Private: Yes, but method is operator-driven; include “Operator procedure” phrasing


---

Example entries

Example A — Caching enabled (Hosted)

Optimization Config updated: Prefix cache enabled for steadier latency

Change summary
- Change ID / Version: ocfg_01J2M7A5ZP2K9R9M1W (previous: ocfg_01J2KX3C8V7Y4T2N0Q)
- Scope: Acme Corp (Hosted), model: redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct, regions: us-east-1
- Effective time (UTC): 2026-02-14 03:12
- Requested by: Acme Corp Admin (jules@acme.example)

What changed
- Caching
  - Prefix/KV cache: Off → On
  - Cache policy: Default → Conservative (evict on high memory pressure)

Why it changed
- Enable caching to reduce repeated-prefill compute and stabilize p95 latency for high-concurrency chat traffic.

Rollout details
- Rollout type: canary
- Canary: 10% for 45 minutes (us-east-1 only)
- Gates used: 5xx rate, p95 latency, GPU utilization
- Result: progressed to 100%

Observed impact (during canary)
- Latency: p95 -6% (p99 -3%)
- Error rate (5xx): no meaningful change
- Cost per 1M tokens: -4% (estimate)

Risk / known limitations
- For very long prompts, caching benefits may be lower; monitoring continues.

Rollback
- Rollback available: Yes
- Rollback method: Console one-click (Optimize > Config History)
- Rollback target: ocfg_01J2KX3C8V7Y4T2N0Q
- Estimated time to take effect: 2–10 minutes

References
- Console link: (placeholder)
- Support: support@redwoodinference.example


Example B — Quant profile change (Dedicated) w/ quality gate

Optimization Config updated: Quantization profile upgraded to Q4_K_M v3

Change summary
- Change ID / Version: ocfg_01J2N0E2D4H1K8QZ3X (previous: ocfg_01J2MZ9W1H7S6P0AAE)
- Scope: Northbridge Analytics (Dedicated), model: redwood/mistral-large, regions: eu-west-1
- Effective time (UTC): Partial rollout (canary)
- Requested by: Redwood Operator

What changed
- Quantization
  - Quant profile: Q4_K_M@v2 → Q4_K_M@v3
  - Safety constraints: Enabled “fallback to fp16 for tool-calling prompts”

Why it changed
- Reduce cost per token while maintaining response quality; change gated by eval harness thresholds.

Rollout details
- Rollout type: staged
- Canary: 5% for 60 minutes (eu-west-1)
- Gates used: 5xx rate, p95 latency, quality eval (prompt set: NBX-Core-Tools)
- Result: paused at 5% (quality gate borderline)

Observed impact (during canary)
- Latency: p95 -2%
- Error rate (5xx): no meaningful change
- Quality: Gate status = Needs review (regression near threshold)

Risk / known limitations
- Tool-calling workloads are sensitive to quantization changes; rollout paused pending evaluation.

Rollback
- Rollback available: Yes
- Rollback method: Console one-click (requires Optimization Change Operator role)
- Rollback target: ocfg_01J2MZ9W1H7S6P0AAE
- Estimated time to take effect: 5–15 minutes

References
- Console link: (placeholder)
- API docs: (placeholder)


Example C — Private deployment (operator-driven rollback language)

Optimization Config updated: Batching limits adjusted for peak throughput

Change summary
- Change ID / Version: ocfg_01J2NY71GQK2V8M9JJ (previous: ocfg_01J2N2K4C1T1Y0ZP7R)
- Scope: Helio Health Systems (Private), cluster: helio-prod, model: redwood/llama-3.1-8b-instruct, region: customer VPC
- Effective time (UTC): 2026-02-10 19:40
- Requested by: Helio Operator

What changed
- Batching
  - Max batch tokens: 8192 → 12288
  - Max batch size (requests): 16 → 32

Why it changed
- Improve throughput during daily peak window; verified against staging load test.

Rollout details
- Rollout type: immediate (operator-managed)
- Gates used: customer monitoring (recommended: 5xx, p95/p99)
- Result: active

Observed impact (first 2h)
- Throughput: +18%
- Latency: p95 +4% (within SLO)

Rollback
- Rollback available: Yes
- Rollback method: Operator procedure (Helm/installer)
- Rollback target: ocfg_01J2N2K4C1T1Y0ZP7R
- Estimated time to take effect: depends on your rollout (typically 10–30 minutes)

References
- Private operator guide: (placeholder)
- Support: support@redwoodinference.example


---

Open questions (need alignment before GA wording)
1) Do we display “who requested” to all roles, or restrict to org admins? Security + privacy check.
2) Should “Observed impact” be optional by default, or always present with “Monitoring ongoing” copy?
3) How do we handle partial rollouts in a single entry?
   - Option A: one entry that updates status over time
   - Option B: separate entries: “Applied (canary started)”, “Promoted to 100%”, “Rollback executed”
4) Do we expose raw config diffs to customers, or only friendly field summaries?
   - If we show diffs, we need a stable public schema + redaction rules.
5) Naming: “Optimization Config” vs “Performance Config” vs “Serving Optimization Settings” (Optimize brand + clarity).
6) For quantization: how much detail about eval sets/metrics do we show without leaking internal methodology?
   - Proposed: show a customer-owned prompt set name if they configured it; otherwise “Redwood standard quality gate”.
7) Rollback semantics statement (runtime): confirm what happens to warmed caches and in-flight requests.


---

Next steps
- Kenji: confirm UI placement and how much text fits in the timeline view; propose “expand details” pattern
- Chloe/Jada: confirm which fields are available from API now vs post-ENG-4828/PM-903
- Sean/Allison: confirm metric windows and wording for impact deltas
- Naomi/Marcus: confirm redaction + visibility rules for actor identity and approval metadata
- Paula: finalize v1 template + copy blocks for “partial rollout”, “paused”, “rolled back” states
